Vanessa / team — thanks for the heads up. From a finance/tax perspective here's the recommended approach and open items: 

Plan (recommended):
- Issue two invoices, one per Starlight legal entity, from the matching Redwood legal entity that has a VAT registration in the relevant country or the EU parent where required. This avoids cross-border VAT misreporting.
- Each invoice will list line-level cost-center codes in a dedicated field so your AP can auto-post.
- Apportionment: prefer to apportion by line-item amounts rather than % at the invoice level — more transparent for audit. If Starlight provides a pre-split, we'll invoice to match.
- Bank details: we need to confirm whether Starlight will do two transfers (one per entity) to our country-specific accounts. If you prefer single remittance, Redwood can accept and perform intercompany netting but that requires a short amendment to the SOW covering settlement responsibilities and likely delays the invoice issue by ~5 business days.

VAT specifics:
- For cross-border B2B services within the EU, in many cases reverse-charge applies. For IT/software/subscription services to an EU-registered VAT business, we generally issue invoices without charged VAT and include the invoicing note (reverse-charge). However, Italy has specific reporting for sales to domestic entities — since one entity is Italy and one Germany, we need to ensure the issuing Redwood entity and presence of a VAT registration matches the required treatment.
- Action item for Elena: please confirm the VAT registration numbers you supplied and whether each entity is VAT-registered for cross-border reverse-charge.

Open items we need from Starlight:
- Confirm whether you want Redwood to apportion amounts or whether you will submit a completed split in the template (preferred by finance).
- Confirm whether you'll make separate remittances.
- Confirm billing contacts for each entity (AP emails).

Once we have those, we'll produce two PDF invoices with the cost-center column and send by May 11 (assuming separate remittances).

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
